   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: C.F. Edwards, WATFORD

Dear Brian,

Congratulations on the standard
and variety of your work. You
must be dedicated. The disks
always arrive in the first few
days of the month, never any
problems with them, everything
loads and runs first time. It
must take a lot of work.

I wrote to you earlier in the
year with a printer problem. You
replied in Issue 47. After try-
ing out your suggestions I still
have not had a lot of luck. You
did say that if I sent a copy of
the relevant page you may be
able to help. This I now do.

The pencilled notes are by the
previous owner who admits he had
problems using the printer with
a SPECTRUM).

Just to recap: The printer is a
SEIKOSHA GP100A. It LLISTs and
LLPRINTs O.K. What I cannot get
is GRAPHICS or the DOUBLE WIDTH
CHARACTER MODE.

             Thanks

          C.F. Edwards

Brian Cavers to C.F. Edwards

The codes on the photocopy seem
to be in hexadecimal so A=10,
B=11, C=12, D=13, E=14 and F=15.

It shows the code for double
width character modes as 0,E so
try LPRINT CHR$ 0;CHR$ 14. To
get back to normal-size text use
LPRINT CHR$ 0;CHR$ 15.The pencil
notes show CHR$ 27 instead of 0
so if it fails try that.

Graphic mode is entered using
LPRINT CHR$ 0;CHR$ 8 but the
page you sent doesn't say in
what form you send the graphics
themselves after entering this
mode. Is there any more info on
that?

Perhaps there  are fixed graphic
characters listed on another
page? Perhaps there is a fixed
length for graphic data. You
could try FOR N=1 TO 8:LPRINT
CHR$ 255:NEXT N: and see what
you get!Perhaps you have to send
the number of graphic bytes
next. You could try...

LPRINT CHR$ 8;CHR$ 0;just before
the above FOR NEXT loop.

Has anyone else got this machine
and can advise?
                        - Brian

From: John Knight, CHELTENHAM

Dear Ron and Brian,

I've got a small problem in that
I want to print out,via Tabloid,
all my back isues but using your
instructions from June '91
(letter to Peter Bell) it does
not work for me. (I've got a
Spectrum 48K+ with +D).

What I'm doing is this:
Show contents. Insert old disc
and load 'A' Editorial.  Nothing
loads here). Insert Tabloid disc
and press T.

           Many thanks,

         John R. Knight

Brian Cavers to John Knight

My instructions to Peter Bell
were for the SAM version. On the
Spectrum version you can load
and print earlier files just by
loading a recent OUTLET to the
CONTENTS page and putting in the
old disc and loading the file.
However, THIS ONLY WORKS BACK TO
ISSUE 36. Before that, filenames
were different. There is no easy
way except this...

Load a recent issue, BREAK and
enter the filename you want,e.g,

300 LOAD "editorialCODE"CODE

          ...then RUN to restart
the program and load as usual.

You can get the filename using
CAT where it is fairly obvious
which file is which.

The word "CODE" within the file-
name is the Sinclair token. If
you have difficulty entering
this (e.g., in 128K mode) then
enter, "editorial" + CHR$ 175.
Note that the token "CODE" is
ALWAYS the TENTH character so
you may need to include spaces,
e.g., "lookout  "+CHR$ 175.
              --
You will need to keep altering
the filename for each text file
you load so, if you are printing
ALL the back issues it might be
easier to do all of one name at
a time, that is, all editorials,
then all letters etc.
                        - Brian

From George Munro, LONDON NW3



Dear Ron and Brian,

Firstly may I wish you and your
respective families a Very Merry
Christmas and a Happiest of New
Years.May I also make a somewhat
selfish and personal wish that
you may both be long spared to
keep up the good work which you
have been doing for so long on
OUTLET!


This letter in addition to its
wishes also contains "good news"
and "bad news". Firstly the good
news...

My +D interface arrived safe and
sound and you will not be
surprised to hear was soon put
to work although it took me some
time to suss it out. This was
not due to it being difficult -
just to my being so dim.

The next good news is that it is
totally compatible with the
SWIFT DISC drives which came
with the SWIFT DISC interface.

[the physical drives only - not
programs saved by SWIFTDISC-BC.]

So, any and all of you SWIFT-
DISCERS out there, grab yourself
a +D interface; not only is it
simple to use but it is very
much faster than SWIFTDISC.

More good news is programs can
be transferred from microdrive
to +D disc but it is a two-stage
procedure:using Romantic Robot's
TRANSEXPRESS one moves the
program from cartridge to tape
then using Outlet's excellent
UNITRANS+ one moves it from tape
to +D disc. The snag of course
is that one has to change
interfaces half way through (see
next paragraph).

The first bad news is it doesn't
work with Interface 1 attached
so when using the +D one cannot
have microdrives at the same
time. I tried Malcolm Goodman's
code in Outlet 40 to make the
Interface 1 "Invisible" but it
didn't seem to fool the +D which
just sat there doing nothing.

The further bad news is that
whilst I was able to transfer
completely the first few OUTLETS
from microdrive to +D disc and
to have them work there, I then
hit a snag. You seemed to have
done something peculiar to your
CONTENTS loader for having
transferred the later issues to
disc I found that when I tried
to run OUTLET from the CONTENTS
page it was moved 4 columns to
the left and the Speccy promptly
locked up.


Please don't advise me to load
the programs from BASIC since
when I do, some will load whilst
others lock the Speccy up with a
black bordered load of nothing.

It may well be that all of this
has already been dealt with by
you in OUTLET and if so just
quote the OUTLET number and
source and I shall trouble you
no more.

One last bit of bad news....

UNITRANS+ does not seem to want
to have anything to do with
"prodata". When I tried to
transfer it to disc from the
tape I had the Error message
"variable not found" which
seemed to refer to a letter and
not a ")"at the end of the code
information.

Can you elucidate please?

Naturally it will not be
necessary to transfer all past
OUTLETS to the new +D system but
I thought it would be interest-
ing to see how far we could
stretch it. The simple answer
will be to select the best
programs from the old microdrive
OUTLETS and transfer them to
stand alone on a new +D disc as
and when they are needed.

The advantage of having both the
+D and the SWIFT DISC systems
will be the ability to transfer
any microdrive program to the +D
disc since SWIFTDISC does run
with INTERFACE 1 in place.

Yours expectantly but mystified,
         George B. Munro


Brian Cavers to George Munro

Thanks, George. I'm glad to hear
you are getting on O.K. with the
+D.

CARTOD in this issue will copy
most files (not BASIC)from cart-
ridge to tape but it's very slow
and TRANSEXPRESS sounds much
better. However, I just rang
Romantic Robot and they do not
sell TRANSEXPRESS any longer.

The Microdrive version of OUTLET
includes special code to handle
two drives - the FAILSAFE code
that you know about. This will
crash on other systems as will
the"off-switch" for this routine
which is in most programs.

To disable this in most programs
just BREAK and check 8940. If
there is a funny calculated POKE
and RETURN there, just enter
8940 RETURN. I say, check the
program because there are one or
two where it wasn't possible to
use that line. You'll still have
problems with NEXT ITEM which
uses PEEK 23728 as a drive flag
and this may crash on +D.

The CONTENTS is more difficult
and I don't recommend trying to
convert it. There are various
problems; you need to remove
CLEARCUT and the two-drive rout-
ines etc. If you want to keep
OUTLET intact it's better to
order the +D versions which are
reduced if you trade in your old
cartridges.

"prodata" is a special data file
made using VARISAVE (OUTLET 26)
which saves the entire variables
area by enclosing it in a giant
string array. To transfer it...

Reset your Spectrum with micro-
drives attached. Enter...

LOAD *"m";1; "prodata" DATA F$()

             and...

SAVE "prodata" F$()

             ...to save to tape.

Reverse that to load back and
save to +D.

                         - Brian

From Brian Gaff to Mr. Cattell


Ah, now that depends on what you
mean by 'support'! All the
boards you mention can be used
by the VTX5000, and all you will
need is scrolling software.


Before I say any more about this
though, a word about the
different types of BB.


The software built into the VTX
5000 is viewdata ONLY. It cannot
be used on scrolling services
because the data is sent in an
8-bit form rather than a 7-bit
one.

Another problem VTX5000 users
can get is line drop. This is
usually because they switch on
line at the start of the
carrier. Most BBs scan other
baud rates, and this can confuse
the VTX, causing line drop. The
best bat is to wait a couple of
seconds, then go on line.

The best scrolling terminal to
get is Specterm 6. I can supply
this, and a selection of other
comms programs for just `1. If
you want a bells and whistles
scrolling terminal, then Dr
Scroll will cost you a fiver,
but it has a userguide.

Now there are Viewdata BBs and
services still operating. Try
these out for size...

This is a subscription service
but has local access.If you join
You can get on as a guest by
entering lots of 4s.


Gnome at Home - 081 888 8894
is a system in decline but can
be fun.


TAO Viewdata - 071 275 9996
is mainly for on-line games but
may expand.

Now there are others but that
will be a start.Tracking working
BBs down is a tiresome business
as nobody tells you when they
close!

Finally, there is a scrolling BB
in Surrey called Infotel that I
can usually be contacted on.
Once you get Specterm, ring 0737
766 027.

My address is in Outboard, as
for BG Services.

                Brian

Brian Cavers to Simon Strange

Well, "user-friendliness" works

Page 41!

Having read it again it seems

up again. You don't say what the

I'm sorry if you had a problem
but I can't guarantee perfection
- I can only guarantee that I
strive and struggle to present
information as clearly as I know
how and double-triple check it!
In any event, I'm ALWAYS willing
to help further if anything is
not clear.

Now, I hope I can help you with
the RS232 problem. Try this...

Enter +3 BASIC from the loader
menu.

MERGE "CONTENTS" (wait a few
seconds until you see "O.K.")

Type: CLS: LIST 1356 then press
ENTER.

When you see the "scroll?" at
the bottom of the screen press
the "N" key.

Press the arrow keys to cursor
up and right/left to move the
editor cursor between the line
number 1356 and FORMAT.

Type: FORMAT LPRINT "R": FORMAT
LINE 9600: then press ENTER (you
must include the final colon :
after 9600 or it will not enter)


The 9600 is the baud rate. Check
your printer to see if it uses a
different baud rate. If so, use
that instead of 9600. It may be
quicker to just try 9600 and see
if it works!

Type RUN 9970 then ENTER to save
this new version of the program
back on the OUTLET disc.

Now type RUN and press ENTER and
try loading a textfile and print
it.

I don't have an RS232 cable so I
can't test this so if anyone
else has done the conversion and
spots a mistake - let us all
know!

Good luck and let me know how
you get on.

                     - Brian.

From: S.D. Trotter, ESSEX

Great mag!I have been a Spectrum
user for many years and I have
been looking for a serious mag
for most of that time;now I have
found one.

Maybe you or one of your readers
can help me with two problems.

Firstly,hardware: I have a large
amount of software,self-written,
which uses Interface 1 ROM calls
so therefore I would like to run
my Interface 1 + microdrive in
parallel with the +D.Obviously a
suitable switching interface is
needed. Is there one available?
Is the switching under software
or hardware control?

Secondly, the software mentioned
above was written with the aid
of the SPECTRUM SHADOW ROM
DISASSEMBLY by Gianluca Carri.


Is such a publication available
for the +D ROM? If not, does
anyone have at least a rough
guide to its working, i.e. entry
and exit addresses, location of
routines, RAM usages for vars,
maps etc., or is this a closely
guarded secret?


I would very much like to conv-
ert my software to the +D so any
help would be greatly appreciat-
ed.

The following is a machine code
print routine which I have found
very useful.  I do not know the
origin of the routine or if it
is widely known but it might
help others.

The routine is called SYS-PT and
should be located where it can
be called from your main machine
code.

This will print to any channel
by first opening the channel
i.e., load the A register with
the channel number and calling
CHANNEL OPEN at #1601 or decimal
5633 in the main ROM.

It will handle any of the PRINT
commands e.g.,AT, INK and PAPER.

In the main code all you have to
do is CALL SYS_PT and then
define the commands and message
followed by 255. This last is
most important as it tells the
routine that you have finished
printing and to return. This is
made in the usual way to the
next command after the 255.


The Listing:-

SYS_PT  EX (SP),HL
        LD A,(HL)
        INC HL
        EX (SP),HL
        CP 255
        RET Z
        RST #10
        JR SYS_PT

On entry, the address of the
last entry on the stack (SP) is
swapped with the contents of the
HL register pair. This is then
incremented and now points to
the first byte of the message.
This is then loaded into the A
register and the incremented
address restored to the stack
pointer in case this is the end
indicator. A test is now made
to see if this is the end
indicator, i.e., 255, and, if it
is, a return is made. If not,
the routine in the main ROM is
called which will print the
contents of the A Register. On
return, a jump is made to SYS_PT
to do the next character.

Example:-

LD A,2         ;Main screen chan
CALL #1601     ;CHAN_OPEN
CALL SYS_PT
DEFB #10,!1    ;INK blue
DEFB #11,#6    ;PAPER yellow
DEFB #16,#A,#A ;AT 10,10
DEFM "This is the main screen"
DEFB #FF       ;255dec.Endmarker
LD A,1         ;Lower screen
CALL #1601
CALL SYS_PT
DEFM "This is the lower screen
DEFB #FF
LD A,3         ;printer
DEFM "This is the printer"
DEFB #FF
This should print to the main
screen, lower screen and printer
if connected. I have found this
very useful and space saving. I
hope you find the same.
                 - S.D. Trotter

Dear Brian,

I was very interested in your
letter to Brian Davies in Issue
52 of OUTLET on +3 disk. My main
interest focussed around the
part that explained how to
connect a 3.5" disk drive to act
as drive B with 706K storage.

I've a Universal 3.5" disk drive
with its own external dip
switches.I'm sure you have come
across this type of drive. The
drive came complete with cable
with edge connector that fits
into the +3's drive B port.

You said in your letter to Brian
Davies that the drive must be
set internally by switch or
jumper to the second drive. Is
this necessary with the Univers-
al drive as the dip switches set
it for Amstrad drive B?


Would I only need BFORMAT(OUTLET
48) to get the drive working
properly with 706k storage?

Could Drive 'B' be made the
default drive and would it then
work with a Multiface to
transfer tape to 3.5" disks (for
back up purposes?) Could the
contents of Drive'A', which is a
3" drive,be transferred to drive
'B' which is now a 3.5" drive?

My second problem is with my
MX8/FT (Epson). When the control
code is set for UNDERLINING in
TEXT I can't get it to STOP
underlining. The other control
codes work perfectly e.g., for
BOLD, ENLARGE, CONDENSED etc. Is
this printer meant to UNDERLINE?
I can't find any mention of this
in the manual. Could anyone help
me with this problem?

P.S. My 3.5" drive is the M.G.T.
Universal drive supplied by EEC
who also sell Q.L. Computers.
When connected up to the +3 the
dip switch must be set for drive
B Amstrad setting. I suppose the
reason for this being that the
+3 disc drive is really an
Amstrad drive.

When connected according to
instructions the MGT 3.5" drive
works pefectly in BASIC but
after formatting the disk there
is only 173k storage available
on the 3.5" disk.

If the 3.5" drive works can
OUTLET be supplied for +3 on
3.5" disk?

        Yours faithfully,

         George Caldwell

Brian Cavers to George Caldwell

No,yes,yes,no,no,yes,yes,no...

No, Brian Gaff's instructions
last month about setting an int-
ernal switch in a second drive
does not apply to the Universal
(or Long Life) drive which, as
you discovered, has an external
setting. It is clear you have it
set up and connected correctly.

Yes,you only need BFORMAT(OUTLET
48) to get 706K on each disc.

Yes,you can then make a'B' drive
the default drive using LOAD"B:"
but no, it will not boot as the
default from the loader menu
which always boots the +3 inter-
nal drive "A".

No, you will not be able to use
Multiface to transfer games
directly to the B drive as the
device always saves to Drive A
but yes, it IS possible to move
them from Drive A to B later
using M3UNLOCK, `9.95 (`6.95 if
you send your own 3" disc) from
TNYSOFT, 27,Baysdale Road,Ashby
Scunthorpe, South Humberside,
DN16 2QE. There's a full review
in OUTLET 40. If ordering, say
you heard about it in OUTLET!

Yes, you can copy the contents
of a disc in Drive A to a disc
in Drive B (and vice-versa so
long as there is room!).However,
use COPY "A:*.*" TO "B:" rather
than COPY "A:" TO "B:" else the
smaller format will be copied
also! (See p.159 +3 manual).

No, OUTLET cannot be supplied in
+3, 3.5" format. Sorry, we don't
have such a set up ourselves and
I'd have a nervous breakdown if
I had one more version of OUTLET
to do! You can copy OUTLET to
3.5" disc of course and the cost
of the 3" OUTLET is the same as
the 3.5" anyway.

The standard Epson code to START
underlining is:- 27, 45,1, i.e.,
LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 45;CHR$ 1.
To STOP underlining is 27,45,0,
(LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 45;CHR$ 0).

If this doesn't work then can
you send me a photocopy of the
pages of your printer manual
relating to underlining, code
lists etc.?
                        - Brian

their staff programmers but who
no longer works with a Spectrum
as far as I know.

However, I've used the program
more or less every week for
nearly 10 years. I thought and
still think it's brilliantly
conceived but not quite so
brilliantly executed, so a year
or so ago I decided to make my
own version of it, with
improvements. I now have:


 1) a complete disassembly of
the original FinMan: fairly
voluminous and perhaps not very
useful, Francis Ainley's
programming is extraordinarily
complicated and quite difficult
to modify.

 2) my own new program, which I
call THE BOOKKEEPER or BK.

BK is a completely new program
using the essential concepts of
FinMan and more or less copying
some of the old menus but not
infringing copyright as it does
not use any of the old coding.

All cartridge/disc handling is
done through BASIC so should
work without modification on any
disc or cartridge system that
uses Microdrive syntax (perhaps
with very small BASIC changes).

Printout is also done through
BASIC, using the LPRINT command
to print a 64-character line
which has been filled by the
machine code.So it ought to work
with any printer which can
handle LPRINT and a 64-character
line.

It can load files made with
FinMan - from cassette tape
only, not from Microdrive or
disc - and vice versa, if you
want to change back. (But BK can
handle larger files than FinMan,
so you might get an overflow.)

I propose to sell BK privately,
for `10 a tape with instructions
but I'm not quite ready yet.
I've been using it myself for
several months, and have had
very useful comments from two
other users who've tried it out.
These will mean writing some new
coding, which will take me a
month or two.

I'd be interested to hear from
Mr. Clay or anyone else who is
interested.     FRANCIS G. MILES

Brian Cavers to Francis Miles



Thanks,Francis. Let us know when

Is such a publication available for the +D ROM? If not, does anyone have at least a rough guide to its working, i.e. entry and exit addresses, location of routines, RAM usages for vars, maps etc., or is this a closely guarded secret?

The following is a machine code print routine which I have found very useful.  I do not know the origin of the routine or if it is widely known but it might help others.

The routine is called SYS-PT and should be located where it can be called from your main machine code.

This will print to any channel by first opening the channel i.e., load the A register with the channel number and calling CHANNEL OPEN at #1601 or decimal 5633 in the main ROM.

It will handle any of the PRINT commands e.g.,AT, INK and PAPER.

In the main code all you have to do is CALL SYS_PT and then define the commands and message followed by 255. This last is most important as it tells the routine that you have finished printing and to return. This is made in the usual way to the next command after the 255.

The Listing:-

SYS_PT  EX (SP),HL LD A,(HL) INC HL EX (SP),HL

```text
        CP 255
```

RET Z RST #10 JR SYS_PT

On entry, the address of the last entry on the stack (SP) is swapped with the contents of the HL register pair. This is then incremented and now points to the first byte of the message. This is then loaded into the A register and the incremented address restored to the stack pointer in case this is the end indicator. A test is now made to see if this is the end indicator, i.e., 255, and, if it is, a return is made. If not, the routine in the main ROM is called which will print the contents of the A Register. On return, a jump is made to SYS_PT to do the next character.

Example:-

LD A,2         ;Main screen chan CALL #1601     ;CHAN_OPEN CALL SYS_PT DEFB #10,!1    ;INK blue DEFB #11,#6    ;PAPER yellow DEFB #16,#A,#A ;AT 10,10 DEFM "This is the main screen" DEFB #FF       ;255dec.Endmarker LD A,1         ;Lower screen CALL #1601 CALL SYS_PT DEFM "This is the lower screen DEFB #FF LD A,3         ;printer DEFM "This is the printer" DEFB #FF This should print to the main screen, lower screen and printer if connected. I have found this very useful and space saving. I hope you find the same. - S.D. Trotter

Dear Ron and Brian,

I'm writing in response to Mr J. Clay's OUTLETTER in OUTLET 52 about Finance Manager +80.

I didn't write FinMan although I did some freelance work for OCP in those good old days. It was written by another Francis, Francis Ainley, who was one of their staff programmers but who no longer works with a Spectrum as far as I know.

Спасибо, George. Рад слышать, что вы успешно осваиваете +D.

Программа CARTOD в этом номере скопирует большинство файлов (кроме BASIC) с картриджа на ленту, но работает она очень медленно, и вариант с TRANSEXPRESS звучит куда лучше. Впрочем, я только что звонил в Romantic Robot, и они больше не продают TRANSEXPRESS.

Версия OUTLET для Microdrive включает в себя специальный код для работы с двумя накопителями — тот самый код FAILSAFE, о котором вы знаете. Он будет сбоить на других системах, равно как и процедура отключения этой подпрограммы («off-switch»), имеющаяся в большинстве программ.

Чтобы отключить это в большинстве программ, просто нажмите BREAK и проверьте строку 8940. Если там находится хитрый вычисляемый POKE и RETURN, просто введите 8940 RETURN. Я говорю «проверьте программу», потому что есть одна или две, где эту строку использовать было нельзя. У вас всё равно останутся проблемы с NEXT ITEM, которая использует PEEK 23728 в качестве флага привода, и на +D это может привести к сбросу.

С CONTENTS всё сложнее, и я не рекомендую пытаться её конвертировать. Там хватает разных проблем: нужно удалить CLEARCUT, процедуры для двух приводов и т.д. Если вы хотите сохранить OUTLET в первозданном виде, лучше заказать версии для +D — они обойдутся дешевле, если вы пришлете взамен свои старые картриджи.

«prodata» — это специальный файл данных, созданный с помощью VARISAVE (OUTLET 26), который сохраняет всю область переменных, упаковывая её в гигантский строковый массив. Чтобы перенести его...

Сделайте сброс Спектрума с подключенными Microdrive. Введите:

```text
LOAD *"m";1; "prodata" DATA F$()
```

и затем...

```text
SAVE "prodata" F$()
```

...чтобы сохранить на ленту.

Для загрузки обратно и сохранения на +D проделайте всё в обратном порядке.

— Brian

Процедура называется SYS-PT и должна располагаться там, откуда её можно вызвать из вашего основного машинного кода.

Она выводит текст на любой канал, предварительно открыв его, т.е. загрузив номер канала в регистр A и вызвав CHANNEL OPEN по адресу #1601 или в десятичном виде 5633 в основном ROM.

Она обрабатывает любые команды PRINT, например AT, INK и PAPER.

В основном коде всё, что вам нужно сделать, это выполнить CALL SYS_PT, а затем определить команды и сообщение, за которыми следует 255. Последнее наиболее важно, так как это указывает процедуре, что печать завершена и пора вернуться. Возврат происходит обычным образом к следующей команде после 255.

Листинг:

```text
SYS_PT  EX (SP),HL
        LD A,(HL)
        INC HL
        EX (SP),HL
        CP 255
        RET Z
        RST #10
        JR SYS_PT
```

При входе адрес последней записи в стеке (SP) меняется местами с содержимым регистровой пары HL. Затем HL увеличивается и теперь указывает на первый байт сообщения. Он загружается в регистр A, а инкрементированный адрес возвращается в указатель стека на случай, если это индикатор конца. Затем проверяется, является ли байт маркером конца, т.е. 255, и если да, то происходит возврат. Если нет, вызывается процедура в основном ROM, которая печатает содержимое регистра A. По возвращении выполняется переход на SYS_PT для обработки следующего символа.

Пример:

```text
LD A,2         ;Main screen chan
CALL #1601     ;CHAN_OPEN
CALL SYS_PT
DEFB #10,!1    ;INK blue
DEFB #11,#6    ;PAPER yellow
DEFB #16,#A,#A ;AT 10,10
DEFM "This is the main screen"
DEFB #FF       ;255dec.Endmarker
LD A,1         ;Lower screen
CALL #1601
CALL SYS_PT
DEFM "This is the lower screen"
DEFB #FF
LD A,3         ;printer
DEFM "This is the printer"
DEFB #FF
```

Это должно вывести текст на основной экран, нижний экран и на принтер, если он подключён. Я нахожу эту процедуру очень удобной и экономящей память. Надеюсь, вам она тоже пригодится.
